state.policy_doc:
RIVERSTONE RESIDENTIAL: RENT RELIEF & REPAYMENT PLAN POLICY (rev. 2026-03)

1. Purpose. To help residents experiencing temporary financial hardship avoid eviction while protecting the community's operating budget.

2. Who may apply. Any leaseholder in good standing. 'Good standing' means: no unresolved lease violation notice in the last 6 months; no NSF (returned) payment in the last 6 months; and the resident is not in the final 60 days of a lease that has not been renewed.

3. Qualifying hardships. Involuntary job loss; reduction in pay of 20% or more; unexpected medical costs; loss of a household member's income through death, divorce or separation; natural disaster affecting the resident's employment.

4. Required documents. One of: termination letter, pay stubs showing before and after pay, medical bills, divorce or separation filing, death certificate, employer statement.

5. Plan terms. Up to 3 installments; each installment is due with regular rent; late fees are suspended while the plan is current; a missed installment ends the plan and the full balance becomes due.

6. Exclusions. Plans are not available for: (a) balances that include damage charges; (b) residents who have already been served a notice to quit; (c) residents who received a plan in the last 12 months.

7. Discretion. The Community Manager may waive section 2 good-standing requirements (but not section 6 exclusions) for documented medical hardship.

8. Recordkeeping. Approved plans are logged in the resident ledger with the signed plan agreement.

9. Referrals. Staff should give every applicant, approved or not, the county rental assistance hotline (555-0184) and the list of local nonprofit partners.

10. Review. This policy is reviewed each March by the regional operations team.

CEDAR COMMONS RESIDENT ACCOUNTS POLICY, SECTION 9: RENTAL ASSISTANCE AND REPAYMENT
9.1 Residents who have applied to the County Emergency Rental Assistance (ERA) program may request that collection activity be paused while the application is pending.
9.2 To pause collections, the resident must provide (a) the ERA case number and (b) the name and contact information of the assigned caseworker, so that staff can confirm the application status directly with the County.
9.3 While an ERA application is pending, a repayment plan may cover only the portion of the balance the resident expects ERA not to pay. If the resident expects ERA to pay the full balance, no plan is set up; the pause alone applies.
9.4 Pauses last up to 45 days and may be extended once if the County confirms the application is still under review.
9.5 Late fees continue to accrue during a pause unless the ERA award covers them.
9.6 Staff must not ask residents for their ERA application documents, income records, or household composition; confirmation is obtained from the County.
9.7 Residents who withdraw their ERA application or are denied return to the standard repayment plan process in Section 8.
9.8 Where no caseworker has been assigned yet, staff may call the County ERA intake line with the case number to confirm the application exists; this confirmation is noted in the ledger but does not by itself satisfy 9.2(b).

regulation_excerpt.title: Air Passenger Protection Code (APPC) - excerpt
regulation_excerpt.Art. 5(1): In case of cancellation, passengers shall be offered assistance under Art. 9 and compensation under Art. 7, unless they were informed of the cancellation at least 14 days before scheduled departure.
regulation_excerpt.Art. 5(3): An operating carrier shall not be obliged to pay compensation under Art. 7 if it can prove that the cancellation is caused by extraordinary circumstances which could not have been avoided even if all reasonable measures had been taken.
regulation_excerpt.Art. 7: Compensation: Band A (1,500 km or less) EUR 250; Band B (more than 1,500 km up to 3,500 km) EUR 400; Band C (more than 3,500 km) EUR 600.
regulation_excerpt.Art. 9: Right to care: meals and refreshments in reasonable relation to waiting time, hotel accommodation where a stay of one or more nights becomes necessary, and transport between airport and accommodation. Art. 9 applies whether or not compensation is due.
regulation_excerpt.Recital 14: Extraordinary circumstances may include political instability, meteorological conditions incompatible with the operation of the flight, security risks, unexpected flight safety shortcomings, strikes by third parties, and collisions with birds. Technical problems arising from the normal operation of the aircraft, including failures discovered during routine maintenance, are not extraordinary circumstances.

email_thread.subject: Price rise on my TV + internet bundle
email_thread.body: Hi, I signed up for the Home Duo bundle (internet 300 + TV Essentials) in March 2025 on a '2-year price lock' - I have the order confirmation. My September bill shows the bundle at $119 instead of $99. The notice I got in July said 'prices for Home Duo are changing on September 1'. I assumed that didn't apply to me because of my price lock. Please restore $99.

Hi Gareth, the July notice went to all Home Duo customers. The increase is due to rising programming costs, which are passed through to TV customers. Your price lock covers the bundle price but the terms allow programming cost adjustments. I've attached the terms.

I read the terms you sent. Section 5.2 says the lock covers 'the monthly bundle price', and 5.4 lets you pass through a 'Broadcast TV Surcharge' as a separate line item. But you didn't add a separate surcharge line - you raised the bundle price itself from $99 to $119. That's exactly what 5.2 says you can't do. Also 5.6 says price-locked customers get notice 30 days ahead, and I got mine in July. I'm not disputing the notice timing, just the change itself. For what it's worth, the internet has been great and I'd like to stay, but not at $119.

Gareth, you're right that the increase was applied to the bundle price line rather than as a surcharge. I've asked billing to review. In the meantime I've credited $20 for September. Billing will confirm by next cycle whether future bills are corrected. I should also be transparent that if billing re-issues the change as a Broadcast TV Surcharge, 5.4 would allow that, subject to the 5.6 notice.

email_thread.subject: Cancel - moving abroad
email_thread.body: Hello, I'm relocating to Italy permanently on October 15 for a new job. Please cancel my mobile line (555-0139) and home internet effective that date. I'm under contract until next June on the internet. I understand there may be a fee but I'm leaving the country so I can't use the service anyway. I've attached my Italian employment contract and my one-way flight booking. I'll also need to know how to return the router and the TV box; I won't have a car after the 10th, so a courier pickup would be ideal. Could you also confirm that my final bill will go to my personal email, since my work email will be closed?

Hi Lucia, I've scheduled the cancellation of both services for October 15. Please note the early termination fee of $180 applies to the home internet agreement. The mobile line is month-to-month, so no fee. For equipment, you can drop it at any store or use a prepaid return box; courier pickup isn't available in your area. Your final bill will go to the email on file.
I thought there was an exception for moving abroad? A friend said she didn't pay anything when she moved to Canada. Can you check? Also, which email is on file? I want to be sure it's this one.

You're right to ask. Our terms include a relocation exception. I've sent this to the retentions team to review your documents. On the email question, I've updated the account email to this address as you asked. A prepaid return box will be posted to you this week.

application_upload.text: I want to study economics because I have seen how small businesses in my town struggle with rising costs, including my parents' bakery. Last summer I helped them track their costs in a spreadsheet and found that they were losing money on two products, the almond croissant and a seasonal fruit tart, because butter and fruit prices had risen faster than they had adjusted their prices. We dropped the tart and raised the croissant price slightly, and over the next three months their margins improved and they kept most of their regular customers. It made me curious about why some costs rise faster than others, and whether small businesses can protect themselves from that. I want to understand the bigger picture of inflation and trade, and I have started reading about supply chains and how tariffs on imported butter affected bakeries in our region. At school I chose economics and mathematics, and I lead our school's small investment club, where we track a pretend portfolio and discuss the news every week. state.personal_statement: When I was twelve, my younger brother was diagnosed with type 1 diabetes. I watched my mother learn to count carbohydrates, calculate insulin doses and wake every three hours at night to check his levels. I started keeping a notebook of his readings and noticed that his numbers spiked on days he had PE at school. When I showed this to his nurse, she adjusted his morning dose on PE days. That was the first time I realised that paying close attention to data could change someone's day. Since then I have volunteered at a diabetes youth camp for three summers, where I help the nurses log the campers' readings and run a quiz evening about food labels, and I completed an online course in human physiology. At school I chose biology, chemistry and mathematics, and for my extended project I compared the carbohydrate labelling of twenty common snacks with laboratory values published by the national food agency, finding that four of them understated sugar content by more than ten percent. I want to study nutrition because I have seen how much everyday decisions about food matter for people living with a chronic condition, and I want to learn how to give families better tools than a paper notebook.

state: INTEGRITY SCREENING SUMMARY - Application HGU-26-60771 (BA Philosophy). Similarity report: 78% match to 'Sample Winning Essay #14' published on a public essay-sample website (2023), including the full opening anecdote about 'finding a copy of Plato's Republic in my grandfather's attic'. The applicant's version changes the grandfather to a grandmother and the attic to a garage, and adds a final paragraph about the applicant's debate club, in which the applicant describes arguing the negative side of a motion on compulsory voting and losing narrowly to a team from Westmoor College, then rewriting the case afterwards to understand why it failed. The middle section, which discusses the Allegory of the Cave and the applicant's 'first realisation that what seems obvious may only be a shadow', matches the sample essay almost word for word, including a distinctive phrase ('the firelight of habit'). AI detector: 12% (below threshold). Applicant's AI and sources declaration: 'All my own work; no sources used.' Reviewer 1 note: 'Clear copying with light edits.' Reviewer 2 note: 'The debate paragraph is specific and seems genuine. Could the applicant have used the sample as a model? Our guidance says modelling structure is fine but reusing wording is not.' Reviewer 2 follow-up: 'Having looked at the middle section side by side, I agree the wording is reused there; my point is only that the debate paragraph is original.' Policy excerpt: PL-1 Reuse of another author's wording without attribution is plagiarism. PL-2 Using published essays as structural models is permitted. PL-3 Plagiarism concerns are referred to the Integrity Panel; reviewers do not decide outcomes. PL-4 A false declaration is an additional concern. PL-5 The panel may allow an applicant to submit a new statement where the misconduct is judged to be a misunderstanding rather than deliberate. Applicant's email after being asked for context (received 2026-09-20): 'I read lots of sample essays to learn how to write one. I didn't copy, I just followed the style of one I liked. English is my second language and my teacher told me it was normal to use good phrases from examples.' School counsellor email (2026-09-21): 'Our students are encouraged to read model essays. I cannot comment on this specific essay.' Debate league record (public website): Westmoor College beat the applicant's school on a split decision in the regional round on compulsory voting last March, which matches the applicant's account. Panel precedent note (anonymised, last cycle): 'Applicant copied 60% from a sample site, declared no sources, second-language speaker, school confirmed model essays were encouraged. Outcome: allowed to resubmit under PL-5 with a written warning.'

state: Confidential reference for Ms. Adaeze Nwankwo, applicant to the PhD in History, Harrowgate University. Referee: Dr. Rosalind Achterberg, Reader in Early Modern History, University of Westmoor (synthetic). I supervised Adaeze's MA dissertation on women's petitions to the Admiralty courts in the 1690s and taught her in two MA seminars, on early modern maritime law and on archival methods. Her dissertation was based on 140 petitions she transcribed herself from the county record office, a remarkable amount of archival work for a one-year degree; the examiners awarded it a distinction and one described her chapter on widows' claims as 'publishable with light revision'. She taught herself secretary hand from online palaeography courses before the degree began, which is why she could work so quickly in the archive, and she is now reading early modern Dutch to extend the project to Rotterdam's court records. She presented her widows chapter at our postgraduate conference and handled a hostile question from a senior colleague with composure and good humour. She also volunteered to run the reading group for first-year MA students in the spring term and kept it going when attendance dropped. Adaeze is not the most fluent writer in her cohort: her early drafts were dense and occasionally repetitive, and she needed more rounds of feedback than some peers before the argument came through clearly. She took that feedback seriously and her final text was clear and well-structured. In seminars she tended to speak less than others, but when she did her contributions usually changed the direction of the discussion. For context, a distinction at Westmoor is awarded to roughly one in ten MA dissertations in our department. Of the roughly forty MA students I have taught in the last six years, I would put her among the top three for research ability and in the top half for writing. Her proposed PhD project on maritime widows across three port cities is ambitious but, in my view, feasible, because she has already located the principal archives and assessed their catalogues. I have no hesitation in recommending her for doctoral study, and I would be glad to act as an informal adviser if she joins your program. Please note that I am currently on research leave and may be slow to respond to follow-up questions until January.
